column1: # One row per builtin behaviour, giving the same computation in BioLang, Python
# and R. The runner generates a single script per language, so adding coverage
# costs a line here rather than three new files — which is what makes covering
# a couple of hundred builtins realistic at all.
# Columns are tab-separated: name, category, biolang, python, r
# An empty r column skips R for that row.
# Python runs with: from Bio.Seq import Seq; from Bio.SeqUtils import gc_fraction
# Values are compared as JSON: floats to 1e-9, integers and strings exactly.

column4: sum(a != b for a, b in zip("ACGT", "ACGT"))
